prompt: Write the body (about 150 words) of an insurer's answer to a personal injury petition in Texas: a general denial and three affirmative defenses that fit a parking lot collision. Plain text. Call the parties only 'Plaintiff' and 'Defendant'. No names, placeholders, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1083; do not mention it.)
text:
Defendant answers Plaintiff's Original Petition by generally denying each and every allegation contained in it, and Defendant demands strict proof of such allegations by a preponderance of the evidence as required by the Texas Rules of Civil Procedure.

For further answer, and without assuming any burden of proof that the law places on Plaintiff, Defendant asserts the following affirmative defenses.

First, Plaintiff's own negligence caused or contributed to the incident. Plaintiff failed to keep a proper lookout, failed to yield the right of way while moving through the parking lot, and failed to maintain a safe speed under the circumstances. Under Chapter 33 of the Texas Civil Practice and Remedies Code, any recovery must be reduced by the percentage of responsibility attributed to Plaintiff.

Second, the injuries and damages claimed were caused, in whole or in part, by a preexisting condition or by a subsequent event unrelated to the incident. Defendant denies that the incident proximately caused the claimed injuries.

Third, Plaintiff failed to mitigate damages by unreasonably delaying treatment or failing to follow medical advice, and any recovery must be reduced accordingly.

Defendant reserves the right to amend this answer as discovery proceeds.
